items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: like Dave Lambert used to sing with V’s

ctx.x: You know I’ve been in some scenarios in which they try to teach jazz vocals and they take, they just have all these almost contrived syllables. And it just doesn’t take on any authenticity.

Well everybody has their own syllables. Some people favor the S sibilance and other people, like Dave Lambert used to sing with V’s, “oh-V-oh-V-oh-V-oh-V-oh” and other people use Bs and whatever works. But you know you have to be telling a story, just as you would on an instrument, because it is your instrument. But I think you can teach jazz up to a point. Well you know, you teach it. But you can only lead them so far. And then something else has to take over.
They say you can lead a sax man to water but you can’t make him gig.
